mcq.q: Target sounds: Which word has the sound /ɔɪ/?
mcq.explanation: Enjoy has the diphthong /ɔɪ/.

mcq.q: Target sounds: Which word has the sound /ɜː/?
mcq.explanation: Girl has the long vowel /ɜː/.

mcq.q: Which word has the long vowel /ɑː/?
mcq.explanation: Market has /ɑː/ in its first syllable.

mcq.q: Target sounds: Which word has the sound /aɪ/?
mcq.explanation: Invite has /aɪ/ in its second syllable.

mcq.q: Which pair is a minimal pair for /l/ and /r/?
mcq.explanation: Lake and rake differ only in the first sound.

mcq.q: To make the /l/ sound, the tip of the tongue
options: stays far from the roof of the mouth and curls back
touches the ridge behind the top front teeth
mcq.explanation: For /l/ the tongue tip touches the ridge and air flows around the sides.

mcq.q: An invitation is
options: a card or message that asks a person to come to an event
mcq.explanation: An invitation invites someone to an event.

mcq.q: Which word means 'to make a place pretty with balloons and ribbons'?
mcq.explanation: To decorate is to make a place look pretty.

mcq.q: Which word means a very big and special meal?
mcq.explanation: A feast is a large special meal.

mcq.q: Which word rhymes with 'road'?
mcq.explanation: Road and load both end with /əʊd/.

mcq.q: Which word has the same vowel sound as 'bird'?
mcq.explanation: Bird and turn both have /ɜː/.

mcq.q: Which of these words has /r/ as its first sound?
mcq.explanation: Ribbon starts with /r/.

mcq.q: Which word has both the sounds /ɔɪ/ and /l/?
mcq.explanation: Oil has /ɔɪ/ followed by /l/.

mcq.q: A simile compares two things using
mcq.explanation: A simile uses like or as, for example as brave as a lion.

mcq.q: Poems and similes: Which sentence has a simile?
options: The runner was as fast as a cheetah.
mcq.explanation: It compares the runner with a cheetah using as ... as.

mcq.q: 'As busy as a bee' means
mcq.explanation: Bees always seem to be working, so it means very busy.

mcq.q: What does the saying 'Unity is strength' mean?
options: People are stronger when they work together
mcq.explanation: Working together makes a group stronger.

mcq.q: 'Practice makes perfect' teaches us that
options: the more we practise, the better we become
practice is a waste of time
mcq.explanation: Repeating a skill helps us improve.

mcq.q: What should you do before you read a story?
options: Read the title and look at the pictures
mcq.explanation: The title and pictures help you predict.

mcq.q: A direct question is one whose answer
mcq.explanation: Direct answers are stated plainly in the text.

mcq.q: Which question is indirect?
options: Why do you think the girl cried?
mcq.explanation: The answer must be worked out from clues.

mcq.q: What does 'Haste makes waste' mean?
options: If you hurry, you may make mistakes and waste things
mcq.explanation: Rushing often leads to errors.

mcq.q: In a readers' theatre, learners
options: read a story aloud with different parts
mcq.explanation: Each reader takes a part and reads the lines.

mcq.q: Poems and similes: Which is a simile?
mcq.explanation: Like a bird compares her singing to a bird's.

mcq.q: 'Sleep like a log' means
mcq.explanation: A log does not move, so it means a deep sleep.

mcq.q: What is the plural of 'box'?
mcq.explanation: Nouns ending in x add es.

mcq.q: What is the plural of 'baby'?
mcq.explanation: A consonant comes before y, so change y to i and add es.

mcq.q: What is the plural of 'monkey'?
mcq.explanation: A vowel comes before y, so just add s.

mcq.q: What is the plural of 'knife'?
mcq.explanation: Change fe to ves.

mcq.q: Which plural is irregular?
mcq.explanation: Child becomes children, not childs.

mcq.q: Which word stays the same in the plural?
mcq.explanation: Sheep is both singular and plural.

mcq.q: What is the plural of 'tooth'?
mcq.explanation: Tooth is irregular.

mcq.q: What is the plural of 'potato'?
mcq.explanation: Some nouns ending in o add es.

mcq.q: What is the plural of 'photo'?
mcq.explanation: Photo just adds s.

mcq.q: Plural nouns: Choose the correct sentence.
mcq.explanation: Women is plural and takes are.

mcq.q: What is the plural of 'leaf'?
mcq.explanation: Change f to ves.

mcq.q: What is the plural of 'church'?
mcq.explanation: Nouns ending in ch add es.

mcq.q: Which noun is always plural?
mcq.explanation: Scissors are two blades joined together, so the noun is plural.

mcq.q: What is the first step in writing a composition?
mcq.explanation: A plan puts ideas in order first.

mcq.q: Which part of a composition tells who, where and when?
mcq.explanation: The introduction sets the scene.

mcq.q: Which is a linking word that shows something happened at the end?
mcq.explanation: Finally introduces the last event.

mcq.q: A new idea in a composition begins
mcq.explanation: Each paragraph holds one idea.

mcq.q: What does 'proofread' mean?
options: Read your work carefully and correct mistakes
mcq.explanation: Proofreading is checking spelling, punctuation and meaning.

mcq.q: Which sentence has correct capital letters and the correct ending?
options: We went to Mombasa on Saturday.
We went to mombasa on saturday
We went to Mombasa on Saturday?
We went to Mombasa on Saturday,
mcq.explanation: Sentences start with a capital letter and names such as Mombasa and Saturday also need capitals.

mcq.q: An open-ended composition
options: gives you a topic and you decide the story
mcq.explanation: You use your own ideas to complete it.

mcq.q: Which is the best way to end a story?
options: With a feeling or a lesson
mcq.explanation: A good ending gives the reader a feeling or a message.

mcq.q: A sentence ends with
options: a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark
mcq.explanation: These are the marks that end sentences.

mcq.q: Which is a good way to make a story interesting?
options: Add small details and one simile
mcq.explanation: Details and similes help the reader picture the story.

mcq.q: 'The sun was as warm as a fresh loaf of bread.' This sentence uses
mcq.explanation: It compares the sun to bread using as ... as.

mcq.q: In a plan for a story, the middle usually tells
mcq.explanation: The middle tells the events, including any problem.

short.q: Write two words with the sound /aɪ/ and use one in a sentence.
short.answer: For example: kite, night. I fly my kite on Saturday.
short.working: 1 mark for two correct words and 1 mark for a correct sentence.

short.q: Write two minimal pairs for /l/ and /r/.
short.answer: For example: light, right and load, road.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct pair.

short.q: Write an invitation of three sentences to a wedding or birthday party, using 'invite' and 'decorate'.
short.answer: For example: I invite you to my sister's wedding on Saturday. We will decorate the hall with flowers. Please come at ten o'clock.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

short.q: Explain how to make the sound /r/.
short.answer: Pull the tongue back a little and curl the tip up without touching the roof of the mouth, and round the lips slightly. The tongue tip touches nothing.
short.working: 1 mark for tongue pulled back, 1 mark for the tip not touching, 1 mark for rounded lips.

short.q: Explain how a word wheel can help you make new words. Give an example with the ending -oy.
short.answer: A word wheel has a fixed ending and different beginning letters. You change the first letter to make a new word. With -oy you can make boy, toy and joy.
short.working: 1 mark for fixed ending, 1 mark for changing the first letter, 1 mark each for two correct words.

short.q: Complete the simile and explain it: 'as cold as ______'.
short.answer: as cold as ice, because ice is very cold.
short.working: 1 mark for a suitable comparison and 1 mark for the explanation.

short.q: Explain what the saying 'A stitch in time saves nine' teaches.
short.answer: It teaches us to fix a small problem early, before it becomes a big problem.
short.working: 1 mark for fixing early and 1 mark for avoiding a bigger problem.

short.q: Give one direct question and one indirect question about a story of a birthday party.
short.answer: Direct: What time did the guests arrive? Indirect: Why do you think the girl was excited?
short.working: 1 mark for each question and 1 mark for correct types.

short.q: Describe three things you do before, while and after reading a story.
short.answer: Before: read the title and predict. While: read slowly and find meanings of new words. After: answer questions and retell.
short.working: 1 mark for each stage.

short.q: Write two sentences using a simile of your own about a celebration.
short.answer: For example: The cake was as sweet as honey. The children danced like leaves in the wind.
short.working: 2 marks for each sentence with a correct simile.

short.q: Write the plurals of: bus, story, wolf, mouse.
short.answer: buses, stories, wolves, mice
short.working: Half a mark for each.

short.q: Give two examples of regular plurals and two of irregular plurals.
short.answer: Regular: books, dishes. Irregular: men, feet.
short.working: 1 mark for each pair.

short.q: Explain the rule for changing nouns that end in y into plurals. Give two examples.
short.answer: If a consonant comes before y, change y to i and add es (baby, babies). If a vowel comes before y, add s (boy, boys).
short.working: 1 mark for each rule and 1 mark for correct examples.

short.q: Rewrite in the plural: 'The child put a loaf and a tomato in the box.'
short.answer: The children put loaves and tomatoes in the boxes.
short.working: 1 mark each for children, loaves and tomatoes and boxes (award 3 for all correct).

short.q: Create a short puzzle with four clues whose answers are irregular plurals.
short.answer: For example: I have two of these and I walk on them: feet. You chew with these: teeth. Small animals that squeak: mice. Grown-up females: women.
short.working: 1 mark for each clue with a correct answer.

short.q: List the three main parts of a composition and say what each does.
short.answer: Introduction: tells who, where and when. Body: tells what happened in order. Conclusion: tells how it ended or how the writer felt.
short.working: 1 mark for each part with its job.

short.q: Write an introduction of two sentences for the topic 'A day I enjoyed'.
short.answer: For example: It was a sunny Sunday in Kisumu. My family went to the lake for a picnic.
short.working: 1 mark for when or where and 1 mark for who or what.

short.q: Give three questions to ask yourself when you proofread.
short.answer: Does every sentence start with a capital letter? Are words spelt correctly? Does my story have a beginning, middle and end?
short.working: 1 mark for each sensible question.

short.q: Make a simple plan for a story called 'The Guests Who Came Late'.
short.answer: Beginning: family prepares for a party. Middle: guests do not arrive, food gets cold. Problem: they lost the way. End: they arrive, everyone laughs and eats.
short.working: 1 mark for a beginning, 1 for events, 1 for a problem and 1 for an ending.

short.q: Explain two ways to make a story interesting.
short.answer: Start with something that makes the reader curious, and add small details or similes. These help the reader picture the story and want to continue.
short.working: 2 marks for each way explained.
